subject: [PATCH v3 2/2] mm/zswap: Support batch writeback in shrink_memcg()

reviews.author: Hao Jia
reviews.summary: Reviewer Hao Jia noted that when list_lru_count_one(nid) < SWAP_CLUSTER_MAX, the current implementation may scan the same entry multiple times within a single pass, and suggested ensuring each entry is scanned at most once per call to avoid this issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Wouldn't it be better to ensure that each entry is scanned at most once 
per call, particularly when list_lru_count_one(nid) < SWAP_CLUSTER_MAX?

On one hand, this avoids scanning the same entry multiple times within a 
single pass. Since the second-chance algorithm rotates referenced 
entries to the tail of the LRU, entries on nodes with a large number of 
zswap entries require at least two shrink_memcg() calls to be written 
back, whereas entries on nodes with fewer entries might get written back 
in a single shrink_memcg() call instead. On the other hand, we also 
avoid spinning repeatedly on entries that fail writeback.

Thanks,
Hao

2026-08-01.patch_summary: This patch modifies the zswap module to support batch writeback in shrink_memcg(). It does this by setting a threshold for the number of pages to be written, allowing for more efficient memory reclaiming. The change involves updating the __list_lru_walk_one function to handle the new threshold.
